metaDescription: Margin leaks differently in every hospitality model. RADR learns where to look — restaurants, hotels, serviced apartments and groups.
heroLead: RADR learns the operating physics of each one.
ctaLead: Open the live demo, or talk to RADR about your locations and stack.

restaurants.problem: More covers can make you less money. Food cost, labor, kitchen throughput, delivery, table turns and guest experience collide during service — demand without contribution is not success.
restaurants.decisions: Hold seating when kitchen load and inbound covers collide. Throttle low-contribution delivery. Feature high €/min dishes under pressure.
restaurants.workRemoved: Floor vs kitchen reconciliation by gut feel, delivery intake without contribution, second-turn surprises.
restaurants.example: D-1911 · Berlin Mitte: Empty tables ≠ capacity. €620 vs seat-now. Wait 12 min. €590 verified protected.

hotels.problem: Fuller does not always mean more profitable. Occupancy and RevPAR can look healthy while contribution deteriorates underneath — channel mix, rate, and readiness rarely sit in one Decision.
hotels.decisions: Hold premium direct vs release OTA. Price remaining inventory to pace. Align housekeeping to contribution, not just fill.
hotels.workRemoved: Occupancy-only brief, OTA dump under event compression, late housekeeping surprises on premium inventory.
hotels.example: D-2201 · 89% occupancy. OTA +11 pts. €4,200 contribution exposure. Hold premium direct — then verify.

bars.problem: Bars & cafés live inside Restaurants & F&B — daypart, waste and weather still follow the same decision loop.
bars.decisions: Staff and stage inventory to weather and daypart. Challenge supplier price books.
bars.workRemoved: Labor-versus-daypart review, supplier price checks, stock-risk monitoring.
bars.example: Warm dry afternoon historically lifts terrace demand — RADR prepares staffing and high-velocity SKUs against the indoor baseline.

groups.problem: Similar revenue. Different profit. Leadership sees locations. They do not always see why similar ADR produces different GOP — labor, channel, supplier, housekeeping and F&B diverge underneath.
groups.decisions: Decompose structural variance into drivers. Verify locally. Roll playbooks across comparable sites.
groups.workRemoved: Ranking without drivers, repeated local interventions, weekly variance archaeology.
groups.example: Amsterdam €214 ADR · 38% GOP vs Berlin €216 ADR · 31% GOP. €14,800 / month structural at risk — local Decision → playbook → group rollout.

finance.problem: Finance & operations is a role, not an industry. RADR separates identified, expected, observed and verified value for every Decision.
finance.decisions: Match invoices to contracts. Chase recoverable credits. Audit Verified Value with proof.
finance.workRemoved: Invoice-to-contract matching, credit chase preparation, verified value tracking.
finance.example: See Verified Value — claim only what you can prove.

apartments.problem: Filling the night can be the wrong Decision. Unit-night economics depend on LOS, turnover, cleaning, channel cost, maintenance and future demand — not simply occupancy.
apartments.decisions: Reject low-quality one-night fill when net contribution after turnover loses to a longer direct path.
apartments.workRemoved: Take-any-booking reflex, channel release guesswork, post-hoc fill analysis.
apartments.example: D-3104 · Booking available. Take-it looks obvious. RADR waits — turnover absorbed, OTA drag, 41% longer direct stay, next-stay Wednesday.
